quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws:

options.text: Is correct because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both drivers and bicyclists can be ticketed if they break traffic laws.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You can only go straight ahead.
You can only go in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go in any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only go in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: The best way to know if you can pass another vehicle is to check:

options.text: If there is a flashing green light ahead.
If the road ahead is straight.
If the vehicle ahead signals that it is okay to pass.
The lane markings on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane markings on the road.
questions.explanation: Lane markings tell you if passing is allowed. A solid line next to your lane means don't pass. You also cannot pass within 100 feet of an intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A lane is ending.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending.
questions.explanation: This warning sign is yellow and black. It tells drivers that a lane is ending and they should prepare for traffic to merge.

questions.question: Which of the following slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision.
Not changing lanes too much.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at collisions causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: A U-turn is not allowed:

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and could cause a crash.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your nerves and body functions. It makes you less careful and harder to concentrate.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver who:

options.text: Is on your left.
Arrived before you.
Is across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the left yields to the one on the right.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the car you passed.
You don't need to use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before you enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before you enter the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. You should be prepared to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase the risk of a crash.
Helps you react faster to dangers.
Often causes drivers to make risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often causes drivers to make risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of car crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky driving decisions.

questions.question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel hard to get back on the road.
Speed up and slowly steer back onto the pavement.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently brake to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels off the road and slow down by gently braking. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back onto the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel hard.

questions.question: At an intersection with a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Let traffic crossing your path go first if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Let only vehicles on your right go first.
Always slow down but you do not have to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic crossing your path go first if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Let other vehicles or traffic cross or merge in front of you. Yield to any traffic that is close enough to create a danger.

questions.question: Drivers should keep a safe distance when driving near a bicycle rider.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Always be careful around cyclists. Keep a safe distance between your vehicle and the bicycle.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The highest safe speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the speed limit for the road. You can drive slower than the posted speed based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign warns you about:

options.text: A road hazard.
An interstate route.
A school crossing.
A speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road hazard.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow warning signs. They alert you to hazards ahead or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A construction worker with a flag is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction worker with a flag is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear bright orange, yellow, or yellow-green clothing. They use paddles and flags to direct traffic and let workers cross the road.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crossings.
On freeway entrance ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crossings.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crossings. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: A railroad crossing sign should be treated like a yield sign.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing sign is a yield sign. You must let any trains and railroad equipment cross before you proceed.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into the right lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: Safely held by a strong adult.
Standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
They won't be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Never standing in the vehicle. They must be properly secured in a seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never standing in the vehicle. They must be properly secured in a seat.
questions.explanation: Small children need special child seats. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper seat to keep children safe.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the road, and the broken line is next to your lane, when may you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
If you are on an expressway.
If the road ahead is clear of oncoming traffic.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road ahead is clear of oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you can pass. You may cross the line to pass only if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You may not park within ____ of an alley entrance, public driveway, or private driveway.

options.text: 10 feet
20 feet
Five feet

questions.correctAnswerText: Five feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within five feet of an alley entrance, public driveway, or private driveway.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity relate to a vehicle's speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make collisions worse. As your speed increases, stopping distance gets longer and collisions become more severe. Keep more distance between your vehicle and others when driving faster.
